Definition: transitive from G1073; to fill entirely:--fill (be) full.
BiblicalUsage: gemízō — fill (be) full. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 8 occurrences, and in Mark, Luke, John, and Revelation the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe gemízō matters because God speaks plainly, and plain words carry real weight. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Calms the Storm; The Wedding Feast; Jesus Turns Water into Wine at Cana
